Interpolate univariate or multivariate time series with missing values

interpol.Rd

Interpolate univariate or multivariate time series with missing values

Usage

interpol(
  incomplete,
  pattern = NULL,
  extend_range = FALSE,
  match = c("position", "name", "stem"),
  interp = c("linear", "stine")
)

Arguments

incomplete

a ts-boxable object with NAs

pattern

a ts-boxable object at the same frequency, or NULL (default) to fill the gaps inside each series by interp. match sets how pattern series pair with the series in incomplete; with "position", a single pattern series serves every series, with a warning. interpol() prints the mapping it uses.

extend_range

logical. If TRUE, the result covers every date of either input, and each series is continued along its pattern over the added dates. If FALSE (default), the result keeps the dates of incomplete.

match

how series in incomplete find their pattern: "position" (default) pairs them in order; "name" needs the same name; "stem" compares names without a final frequency or solution ending, as in chain(), so VISNS_HI_Q pairs with VISNS_HI_M. With "name" or "stem", every series needs a partner, or interpol() stops. A single series in each always pairs.

interp

without a pattern: "linear" (default) fills a gap along a straight line, "stine" along a Stineman spline through the observed values, which bends smoothly without overshooting them (as in extend()). With a pattern only "linear" is allowed; "stine" is an error.

Value

interpolated object of the same type as the input

Details

With a pattern, a gap inside a series follows the pattern's growth from the last known value, plus a correction that grows linearly across the gap so the path ends on the next known value. A gap at the start or end of a series follows the pattern's growth from the nearest known value. Where the pattern is NA, or does not cover a gap's end points, the gap stays NA.

Without a pattern, missing values between a series' first and last observation are filled by interp (by position, so each period counts the same); missing dates in a regular series are added first, and leading and trailing gaps stay empty. extend_range has no effect then.

Examples

# straight-line fill of an internal gap
make_xts("2025M7", val = c(1, 2, NA, 4, 5)) |>
  interpol()
#>            value
#> 2025-07-01     1
#> 2025-08-01     2
#> 2025-09-01     3
#> 2025-10-01     4
#> 2025-11-01     5
# a smooth fill along the curve of the neighbouring values
make_xts("2025M7", val = c(1, 1.2, 2, NA, NA, 8, 8.5)) |>
  interpol(interp = "stine")
#>               value
#> 2025-07-01 1.000000
#> 2025-08-01 1.200000
#> 2025-09-01 2.000000
#> 2025-10-01 3.746101
#> 2025-11-01 6.275314
#> 2025-12-01 8.000000
#> 2026-01-01 8.500000
monthly_data_example |>
  dplyr::filter(time > "2002-01-01") |>
  tsbox::ts_long() |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    value = dplyr::if_else(time > "2021-01-01" & time < "2022-01-01",
    NA_real_, value)
  )|>
  interpol(monthly_data_example, extend_range = TRUE) |>
  span("2020-11-01", "2022-02-01")
#> The mapping between interpolated series and pattern series is the following:
#>  VISNS_HI_I  VAPNS_HI_I VADCNS_HI_I 
#>  VISNS_HI_P  VAPNS_HI_P VADCNS_HI_P 
#> # A tibble: 48 × 3
#>    id       time       value
#>    <chr>    <date>     <dbl>
#>  1 VISNS_HI 2020-11-01  184.
#>  2 VISNS_HI 2020-12-01  237.
#>  3 VISNS_HI 2021-01-01  172.
#>  4 VISNS_HI 2021-02-01  235.
#>  5 VISNS_HI 2021-03-01  440.
#>  6 VISNS_HI 2021-04-01  485.
#>  7 VISNS_HI 2021-05-01  630.
#>  8 VISNS_HI 2021-06-01  792.
#>  9 VISNS_HI 2021-07-01  880.
#> 10 VISNS_HI 2021-08-01  723.
#> # ℹ 38 more rows
monthly_data_example |>
  tsbox::ts_long() |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    value = dplyr::if_else(
      time > "2021-01-01" & time < "2022-01-01",
      NA_real_,
      value
    )
  ) |>
  interpol(
    # missing values in the pattern
    monthly_data_example |>
      tsbox::ts_long() |>
      dplyr::mutate(
        value = dplyr::if_else(
          time > "2021-03-01" & time < "2021-09-01",
          NA_real_,
          value
        )
      )
  ) %>%
  # no interpolation where pattern has NAs (April to August 2021)
  tsbox::ts_wide() |>
  span("2020-11-01", "2022-02-01")
#> The mapping between interpolated series and pattern series is the following:
#>  VISNS_HI_I  VAPNS_HI_I VADCNS_HI_I 
#>  VISNS_HI_P  VAPNS_HI_P VADCNS_HI_P 
#> # A tibble: 16 × 4
#>    time       VISNS_HI VAPNS_HI VADCNS_HI
#>    <date>        <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
#>  1 2020-11-01     184.     226.      76.2
#>  2 2020-12-01     237.     289.      94.7
#>  3 2021-01-01     172.     227.      80.8
#>  4 2021-02-01     235.     272.      90.7
#>  5 2021-03-01     440.     492.     137. 
#>  6 2021-04-01      NA       NA       NA  
#>  7 2021-05-01      NA       NA       NA  
#>  8 2021-06-01      NA       NA       NA  
#>  9 2021-07-01      NA       NA       NA  
#> 10 2021-08-01      NA       NA       NA  
#> 11 2021-09-01     505.     597.     154. 
#> 12 2021-10-01     551.     660.     165. 
#> 13 2021-11-01     614.     714.     191. 
#> 14 2021-12-01     753.     838.     247.
